transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve kind of stopped caring about things I used to do to keep myself steady. Sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society, even working in the woodshop—it all just feels like another chore now, and I keep putting it off.
Have you noticed that you no longer enjoy activities that you used to find pleasurable or rewarding, like sailing or working in the woodshop?

Yeah… I have. That’s probably what finally got me to come in. Sailing, the historical society on Saturdays, even messing around in the woodshop… they used to help, I guess. Now they just feel like things I’m supposed to do, and I keep putting them off.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?
I don’t know if I’d call it depressed most of the day. I’ve been… off, I guess. But I haven’t really been keeping track like that.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?
I’m still not sure. I’ve had rough patches, but “most of the day, nearly every day”... I don’t know that I can say that.
Can you think back to how you’ve been feeling over the last two weeks—have there been days where you felt down or sad most of the day, even if it wasn’t all day every day?
Maybe a couple days were like that, yeah. Not the whole day exactly, but a lot of it. I mostly just kept to myself and got through what I had to do.
Can you clarify if, on those days when you felt down, it lasted for most of the day, and whether these days were spread out over the past couple of weeks?
I’m not really sure. A couple days, yeah, I felt low for a good stretch, but I didn’t watch the clock or anything. They were kind of scattered, I think… not every day.
On the days when you felt down, did that low mood last for most of the day, or did it come and go in shorter periods?

It’s more… in the background, I guess. It comes and goes some, but there’s this low dread and guilt that kind of follows me around, like I should’ve caught one more risk, even though people say the controls were there.
Have you noticed a decrease in your interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like sailing, working at the historical society, or spending time in the woodshop?

Yeah… I guess that’s part of why I agreed to come in. The stuff that used to keep me steady—sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society, even messing around in the woodshop—it just feels like another chore now. I keep putting it off.
Can you tell me if this low mood or background feeling of dread has been present for at least two weeks straight, even if it’s not constant throughout the day?

Yeah… I think so. Not every minute, but for at least a couple weeks there’s been this low-grade dread and guilt hanging around. Like I should’ve seen one more risk coming, even though people keep telling me the controls were in place.

Can you tell me if you’ve completely lost interest in doing any of the activities you used to enjoy, like sailing or working in the woodshop, or if you still have some interest but just don’t feel like doing them anymore?

I wouldn’t say it’s completely gone, exactly. It’s more like… I know those things used to matter—sailing, the historical society, the woodshop—but right now I just don’t care enough to actually do them. They feel like chores, so I keep putting them off.
Over the past two weeks, have you had days where your mood was down or depressed for most of the day, and if so, how often did that happen?

Yeah… most days, I’d say. It’s not like I’m crying all day or anything, but there’s this background dread and guilt that hangs around. Like I should’ve caught one more thing, even though everyone says the controls were in place.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in most or all activities, not just the ones you used to enjoy like sailing or the woodshop?

Mostly the things that used to keep me steady, I guess. Sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society… even the woodshop. I wouldn’t say absolutely everything, but those all just feel like chores now, and I keep putting them off.
Have you found that you no longer take pleasure in most things you used to enjoy, not just sailing, the historical society, or the woodshop?

Yeah… I guess so. It’s mostly that the things that used to keep me balanced just don’t do much for me now. The races, the historical society, tinkering in the shop… I keep telling myself I’ll get back to them, but they just feel like work.
Over the past two weeks, has your mood been down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… nearly every day, I think. It’s more this low-grade dread and guilt that just kind of follows me around. Like I should’ve seen one more risk coming, even though people keep saying the controls were there.
Over the past two weeks, have you had days where your mood was down or depressed for most of the day, and if so, how often did that happen?

Most days, yeah. It’s not always dramatic, but it sits there most of the day… this dread, and guilt. Like I missed something I should’ve caught, even if people keep telling me the safeguards were there.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… I’ve answered that already, but yes. Most days it’s there for most of the day. Just this low dread and guilt, like I should’ve caught one more thing, even if everyone says the controls were in place.
Have you found that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in almost all of your usual activities, not just the ones you’ve mentioned like sailing or working in the woodshop?

Yeah. It’s… broader than just those. The sailing races, the historical society shift on Saturdays, even going out to the woodshop—those used to steady me a bit. Now they just feel like obligations I keep putting off. That’s part of why I finally agreed to come in.
Over the past two weeks, have you noticed a decrease in your energy levels or felt more fatigued than usual, even when you’re not doing much physically?
I don’t know… not in a way I’ve really tracked. I get tired, sure, but I couldn’t say it’s been a clear drop in energy.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt unusually tired or noticed a clear drop in your energy levels, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?
Not really clear, no. I mean, I get tired like anyone, but I haven’t noticed some big drop in energy just sitting around or anything.
